test_title: PYST 09: SSC Stenographer 2025: General Awareness (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question: India's improvement in the Rule of Law Index is most critically challenged by which factor?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Slow judicial delivery**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Slow judicial delivery** is one of the most critical issues affecting India's Rule of Law Index ranking.
 
• India's judicial system is burdened with a massive backlog of cases—over 4.5 crore cases were pending in courts as of 2023, according to the National Judicial Data Grid.
 
• The average time to resolve cases in lower courts is several years, while higher courts may take decades to deliver final judgments.
 
• The delay leads to a lack of trust in the justice system, undermining the effectiveness of the Rule of Law in ensuring accountability and fairness.
 
• Factors contributing to slow judicial delivery include insufficient judicial workforce, underfunded courts, procedural complexities, and lack of technological integration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rule of Law Index**

 
 
• The Rule of Law Index is published by the World Justice Project (WJP) and measures how the rule of law is experienced and perceived globally.
 
• The index evaluates factors such as constraints on government powers, absence of corruption, open government, and access to justice.
 
• India ranked 77th out of 140 countries in the 2022 Rule of Law Index.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Backlog in India**
 
 
• As of 2023, over 4.5 crore cases were pending, with nearly 90,000 cases in the Supreme Court alone.
 
• The Law Commission of India has repeatedly recommended increasing the number of judges to address the backlog.
 
 
 
• **National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG)**
 
 
• An online platform that provides real-time data on pending and disposed cases in Indian courts.
 
• It aims to promote transparency and enable better management of case workloads.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Reforms**
 
 
• Proposed reforms include hiring more judges, adopting Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) mechanisms, and leveraging technology for e-courts.
 
• The E-Courts project is being implemented under the Digital India program to ensure faster and more transparent justice delivery.
